passages.text: For most of recorded history, lending money at interest was not a business but a sin. The prohibition was no eccentricity of a single religion: it appears in Jewish, Christian and Islamic law, and Aristotle had argued for it centuries earlier on the ground that money is barren and cannot breed. The argument was more serious than it now sounds. In an economy where almost all borrowing was distress borrowing, brought on by a bad harvest, a funeral or a debt to a landlord, a loan at interest moved money from somebody who had nothing to somebody who had a great deal, and the moral objection followed the economic reality closely. What changed was not the ethics but the borrower. Once loans were taken out to finance a voyage or a workshop rather than to survive a winter, the lender was no longer exploiting a need; he was sharing a risk, and a share of the gain looked a good deal less like theft. Lawyers reached this conclusion long before any theologian conceded it, by devising contracts that were interest in everything but name. The prohibition did not so much collapse as get walked around, and the routes are still visible in the vocabulary of modern finance. What survives of the old argument is the word usury itself, which no longer means lending at interest but lending at a rate somebody considers excessive. That shift is not a defeat of the idea. It is the idea being narrowed until it fits an economy that could not exist without the thing it once forbade.

The word wilderness suggests a place where human beings have never been, and almost nowhere it is applied answers that description. The great national parks of North America, which supplied the modern image of untouched nature, had been shaped for thousands of years by the people who lived in them, chiefly through fire: burning the undergrowth kept the forest open, encouraged the plants that game animals fed on, and prevented the accumulation that makes a very large fire possible. Those people were removed, in some cases by force, and the landscape that was then photographed and protected was not an ancient one but a recent one, produced by their absence. The protection itself completed the change. Fire was suppressed as a matter of policy, the undergrowth came back, and within a century the parks were burning in a way nobody had ever recorded. The managers who eventually reintroduced controlled burning were reproducing, at considerable expense, a practice their predecessors had spent decades preventing. None of this is an argument against protecting land, and it is regularly mistaken for one. It is an argument against a particular idea of what is being protected. A landscape maintained by people for millennia is not worth less than one that was never touched; it is simply a different thing, and it asks for management rather than abstention. The word gets in the way because it carries a promise that the place can be left alone, and the places we have given the name to are mostly places that cannot.

Games are old; rules that travel are not. Football of a kind had been played in English villages for centuries, and what was played in one village could not be played against the next, because nobody had written anything down and every settlement's version was slightly different. The codification that took place in the middle of the nineteenth century was not an improvement of these games but a condition for a new kind of contest: a match between strangers. Written rules made it possible to play against somebody you had never met, which in turn made leagues, records and national teams thinkable. The people who wrote the rules were schoolmasters and clerks, and the codes carry their preoccupations. The distinction between the amateur and the professional, which looks like a point of sporting ethics, was in its origin a mechanism of class: a man who could not afford to lose a day's wages was unable to play unless he was paid, so a rule against payment was a rule against his presence. It was defended for eighty years in the language of purity and abandoned without much ceremony once the crowds were large enough to matter. The codes also fixed things nobody now thinks of as decisions at all: the size of the pitch, the number of players on each side, the length of the match. None of these follows from the game. They follow from a committee, usually in a single meeting, and they have survived every later revision because by the time anybody thought to question them they had become what the game was.

Until surprisingly recently, prison was not a punishment. It was a place where the accused waited for a trial, or the convicted waited for the punishment itself, which was a fine, a whipping, transportation or death. The idea that a court should sentence somebody to a quantity of time is about two hundred years old, and it required two things that had not previously existed: a state able to feed and guard large numbers of people for years, and a shared sense that time is a measurable thing which can be taken from a person in units. The second is easy to overlook. A sentence of four years means very little in a society without clocks, calendars and wages paid by the week. Once the idea had arrived it spread with remarkable speed, partly because it looked humane beside the alternatives and partly because it was administratively convenient: it could be graded, appealed against, reduced and recorded, which a whipping cannot. Its critics have always made the same two objections, and both survive. The first is that the unit is not equal, since a year takes more from a young person than from an old one and more from somebody with dependants than from somebody without, so that the same sentence is a different punishment for different people. The second is that nobody has ever been able to say what a year is supposed to accomplish. The sentence is precise about quantity and silent about purpose, and two centuries have not filled the silence.

A company's accounts are public today because companies once collapsed with nothing to show. The limited liability company, which allowed an investor to lose only what he had put in, made it possible for strangers to finance an enterprise they could not supervise, and the same feature made it possible for a promoter to raise money for an enterprise that did not exist. The nineteenth century produced a long series of such collapses, each followed by an inquiry, and the requirement to publish audited accounts was assembled out of those inquiries rather than designed in advance. This origin explains a great deal about what the accounts do and do not tell a reader. They were built to answer the question the collapses had raised, which was whether the money is there, and they answer it well. They were not built to say whether a business is well run, and they say very little about it. A firm can satisfy every requirement and be failing; another can look alarming and be perfectly sound. The auditor's report is often read as a verdict on the company, and it is nothing of the kind: it says that the statements are consistent with the records, which is a far narrower claim than almost any reader assumes. The gap between what the document certifies and what it is taken to certify has produced most of the scandals of the last century, and each of them has been followed by a demand for more disclosure rather than for a different kind of question.

questions.stem: Although the prohibition on lending at interest appears in three separate legal traditions and was defended by Aristotle as well, ----.

options.o1: it was walked around for centuries before anybody formally abandoned it
options.o2: it was formally abandoned long before anybody thought of walking around it
options.o3: medieval lawyers were the first to state it in its strongest form
options.o4: the borrowing it forbade was almost always undertaken out of need
options.o5: the word usury has kept its original meaning down to the present day

questions.why: Ödün bağlacı, yasağın gücüne rağmen ne olduğunu ister: yasak kaldırılmamış, etrafından dolaşılmıştır.
questions.trap_note: İki olayın sırasını ters çevirir; dolanmak resmî kaldırmadan sonra değil, çok önce gelmiştir.

questions.stem: As long as almost every loan was taken out by somebody who could not afford a bad harvest, ----.

options.o1: the moral objection to interest matched the economic facts fairly closely
options.o2: the moral objection to interest had very little to do with the economic facts
options.o3: lenders were sharing a risk rather than exploiting anybody's need
options.o4: the contracts devised by medieval lawyers were entirely unnecessary
options.o5: the rate charged mattered a good deal more than the loan itself

questions.why: As long as bir koşul kurar: borçlanma zorunluluktan doğduğu sürece ahlaki itiraz ekonomik gerçekle örtüşür.
questions.trap_note: İlişkiyi koparır; oysa koşul cümlesi tam da itirazın neden yerinde olduğunu açıklamak için kurulmuştur.

questions.stem: So completely were the original inhabitants removed from the land that later became a national park ----.

options.o1: that the landscape photographed there was a recent product of their absence
options.o2: that the landscape photographed there had survived untouched for millennia
options.o3: and the fires they had set every season went on exactly as before
options.o4: because the park authorities wanted the forest to remain open
options.o5: so the undergrowth was burned off at regular intervals after all

questions.why: So + zarf devrik yapısı bir derece-sonuç ilişkisi kurar ve that ile tamamlanır; sonuç, manzaranın yokluktan doğmuş olmasıdır.
questions.trap_note: Yapıyı doğru tamamlar ama parçanın düzelttiği yanılgıyı tekrarlar: manzara eski değil, yenidir.

questions.stem: The park managers who eventually reintroduced controlled burning, a century after fire had been suppressed as a matter of policy, were ----.

options.o1: restoring at great cost a practice their predecessors had spent decades suppressing
options.o2: introducing a practice that had never been used on that land before
options.o3: reducing the number of visitors admitted to the parks each season
options.o4: photographing a landscape that had not changed for thousands of years
options.o5: removing the inhabitants who had managed the forest before them

questions.why: Yakmanın yeniden getirilmesi, daha önce bastırılan bir uygulamanın pahalı biçimde geri alınmasıdır.
questions.trap_note: Uygulamayı yeni sanır; oysa parça onu binlerce yıllık bir alışkanlık olarak tanıtır.

questions.stem: Had the rules of football never been written down in the middle of the nineteenth century, ----.

options.o1: a match between two villages that had never met would have been impossible
options.o2: the game would have gone on being played in the same way in every village
options.o3: leagues and national teams would have appeared a good deal sooner
options.o4: the distinction between amateur and professional was a matter of class
options.o5: schoolmasters and clerks will not be remembered for having written them

questions.why: Had + özne + V3 if'siz üçüncü tip koşuldur ve ana cümle would have + V3 ister; sonuç yazılı kural olmadan yabancıyla maçın olanaksızlığıdır.
questions.trap_note: Yazısızlığın sonucunu tekdüzelik sanır; parça her köyün sürümünün biraz farklı olduğunu söyler.

questions.stem: Since a man who could not afford to lose a day's wages was unable to play unless he was paid for it, ----.

options.o1: a rule forbidding payment was in effect a rule forbidding his presence
options.o2: a rule forbidding payment was defended as a matter of sporting ethics
options.o3: the size of the pitch and the number of players were fixed by a committee
options.o4: professional players were admitted to the game some eighty years later
options.o5: the crowds eventually grew large enough for the question to matter

questions.why: Since bir gerekçe kurar ve sonucu belirler: ödemeyi yasaklamak, ödeme olmadan oynayamayacak olanı dışlamaktır.
questions.trap_note: Doğru bir bilgidir ama sonuç değildir; kuralın nasıl savunulduğu, kimi dışladığını söylemez.

questions.stem: Not only was a sentence of imprisonment easier to grade, to record and to reduce than a whipping had ever been, ----.

options.o1: but it also struck contemporaries as the more humane of the two
options.o2: but it was also a great deal cheaper for the state to administer
options.o3: and courts had been sentencing people to it for many centuries
options.o4: so the accused no longer had to wait in prison for a trial
options.o5: although the length of the sentence was decided by the sheriff

questions.why: Not only ... but also kalıbı ikinci bir üstünlük ister; parçada hapsin yayılma nedenleri idari kolaylık ve insani görünmesidir.
questions.trap_note: Ucuzluk iddiası parçayla çelişir: hapis, binlerce kişiyi yıllarca besleyip gözetebilen bir devlet gerektirir.

questions.stem: However precisely a court specifies the number of years a prisoner is to serve, and however carefully that number is arrived at, ----.

options.o1: it says nothing at all about what those years are meant to achieve
options.o2: it states quite clearly what those years are expected to achieve
options.o3: the sentence is reduced automatically after a fixed period has passed
options.o4: prisons were originally places where the accused waited for a trial
options.o5: the state must be able to feed and guard him for the whole of it

questions.why: However + zarf bir ödün kurar: ölçüdeki kesinlik ne olursa olsun amaç konusundaki sessizlik sürer.
questions.trap_note: Ödünü tersine çevirir; parça cezanın nicelikte kesin, amaçta sessiz olduğunu söyler.

questions.stem: The requirement to publish audited accounts was put together out of a long series of inquiries into company collapses, ----.

options.o1: which is why it answers one question thoroughly and others hardly at all
options.o2: which is why it was designed from the outset as a complete system
options.o3: although limited liability had been introduced a good deal earlier
options.o4: so investors were at last able to supervise the firms they financed
options.o5: even though auditors had objected to the requirement for years

questions.why: Soruşturmalardan derlenmiş bir yükümlülük, o soruşturmaların sorduğu soruyu yanıtlar ve başka soruları yanıtsız bırakır.
questions.trap_note: Derlenmiş olmakla tasarlanmış olmayı karıştırır; parça bunları birbirine karşıt kurar.

questions.stem: Because an auditor certifies only that the statements agree with the records kept by the company itself, ----.

options.o1: a clean report is not the verdict on the business that readers take it for
options.o2: a clean report is the strongest verdict on a business that can be given
options.o3: the accounts of a failing firm will generally fail the audit as well
options.o4: every scandal of the last century has followed from a false record
options.o5: the demand after each collapse has been for rather less disclosure

questions.why: Denetimin kapsamı dar olduğuna göre temiz bir rapor, işin iyi gittiğine dair bir hüküm sayılamaz.
questions.trap_note: Dar bir teknik onayı en güçlü hükme çevirir; parçanın bütün savı bu okumaya karşıdır.

questions.stem: What survives of the old argument is the word usury itself, which no longer means lending at interest but lending at a rate somebody considers excessive.

options.o1: Eski tartışmadan geriye kalan, usury sözcüğünün kendisidir; bu sözcük artık faizle borç vermek değil, birilerinin aşırı bulduğu bir oranla borç vermek anlamına gelir.
options.o2: Eski tartışmadan geriye kalan, usury sözcüğünün kendisidir; bu sözcük artık birilerinin aşırı bulduğu bir oranla değil, faizle borç vermek anlamına gelir.
options.o3: Usury sözcüğü eski tartışmanın tek kalıntısıdır ve anlamı yüzyıllardır hiç değişmemiştir.
options.o4: Faizle borç vermenin aşırı sayılıp sayılmadığına karar veren şey, usury sözcüğünün eski anlamıdır.
options.o5: Eski tartışma sürmektedir, çünkü hangi oranın aşırı olduğu konusunda anlaşma sağlanamamıştır.

questions.why: not X but Y kalıbı eski anlamı dışlar, yeni anlamı koyar; çeviri bu sırayı korumalıdır.
questions.trap_note: Kalıbın iki ucunu değiştirir ve sözcüğe tam da bıraktığı anlamı geri verir.

questions.stem: Nowhere that the word wilderness is applied does it describe a place where human beings have never been.

options.o1: Wilderness sözcüğünün kullanıldığı hiçbir yer, insanın hiç ayak basmadığı bir yeri anlatmaz.
options.o2: Wilderness sözcüğünün kullanıldığı her yer, insanın hiç ayak basmadığı bir yeri anlatır.
options.o3: İnsanın hiç ayak basmadığı yerler için wilderness sözcüğü kullanılmaz olmuştur.
options.o4: Wilderness sözcüğü, insanın ayak bastığı yerlerde kullanıldığında yanlış anlaşılmaktadır.
options.o5: İnsanın hiç ayak basmadığı yerlerin sayısı, wilderness denen yerlerin sayısından azdır.

questions.why: Nowhere cümle başına gelince devrik yapı kurulur ve mutlak bir olumsuzluk bildirir: hiçbir örnekte böyle değildir.
questions.trap_note: Devrikliği vurgu sanıp olumsuzluğu düşürür; cümle bu kez tam tersini söyler.

questions.stem: The rule against payment was defended for eighty years in the language of purity and abandoned without much ceremony once the crowds were large enough to matter.

options.o1: Ödeme yasağı seksen yıl boyunca saflık diliyle savunuldu ve kalabalıklar önemsenecek kadar büyüyünce fazla tören yapılmadan terk edildi.
options.o2: Ödeme yasağı seksen yıl boyunca terk edildi ve kalabalıklar önemsenecek kadar büyüyünce saflık diliyle savunulmaya başlandı.
options.o3: Kalabalıklar büyüdükçe ödeme yasağı daha da sıkı biçimde savunuldu ve seksen yıl sonra kaldırıldı.
options.o4: Saflık dili, ödeme yasağının kalabalıklar küçüldüğünde terk edilmesini engelledi.
options.o5: Ödeme yasağı, saflığı savunanlarla kalabalığı savunanlar arasında seksen yıl süren bir tartışma yarattı.

questions.why: Cümlede iki edim sırayla verilir: önce uzun bir savunma, sonra sessiz bir vazgeçiş.
questions.trap_note: İki edimin yerini değiştirir; aynı sözcüklerle olayların sırası tersine döner.

questions.stem: Hapsin bir ceza sayılabilmesi için, zamanın kişiden birimlerle alınabilen ölçülebilir bir şey olduğu düşüncesinin önce yerleşmesi gerekiyordu.

options.o1: Before imprisonment could count as a punishment, the idea that time is a measurable thing which can be taken from a person in units had first to take hold.
options.o2: Once imprisonment had come to count as a punishment, the idea that time is a measurable thing which can be taken from a person in units began to take hold.
options.o3: Imprisonment counted as a punishment only in societies that had clocks, calendars and weekly wages.
options.o4: The idea that time can be taken from a person in units was invented in order to justify imprisonment.
options.o5: Time could not be measured in units until imprisonment had become the ordinary form of punishment.

questions.why: Türkçe cümle bir önkoşul kurar: düşünce önce yerleşmeli, hapis ancak ondan sonra ceza sayılabilir.
questions.trap_note: Önkoşulu sonuca çevirir; hangi olayın önce geldiği değişince cümlenin savı ortadan kalkar.

questions.stem: Denetçi raporu şirket hakkında bir hüküm sanılır; oysa söylediği yalnızca tabloların kayıtlarla tutarlı olduğudur.

options.o1: The auditor's report is taken for a verdict on the company, whereas all it says is that the statements are consistent with the records.
options.o2: The auditor's report is taken for a statement that the accounts are consistent with the records, whereas it is in fact a verdict on the company.
options.o3: The auditor's report says both that the statements are consistent with the records and that the company is sound.
options.o4: Readers of an auditor's report are rarely told which records the statements were compared with.
options.o5: A verdict on a company cannot be given until its statements have been compared with its records.

questions.why: Cümle bir sanı ile gerçeği karşı karşıya koyar: sanılan hüküm, söylenen ise dar bir tutarlılık saptamasıdır.
questions.trap_note: Sanı ile gerçeği yer değiştirir; kalıp korunduğu için cümlenin tersi doğru gibi okunur.

questions.stem: Her çöküşün ardından daha fazla açıklama istendi, farklı türden bir soru sorulması değil.

options.o1: After every collapse what was demanded was more disclosure, not a different kind of question.
options.o2: After every collapse what was demanded was a different kind of question, not more disclosure.
options.o3: Every collapse was followed by a demand for fewer disclosures and for different questions.
options.o4: The questions asked after a collapse were always the same, however much was disclosed.
options.o5: More disclosure was demanded only where a different kind of question could not be asked.

questions.why: Türkçe cümlede istenen açıklamadır; istenmeyen ise soru türünün değişmesidir.
questions.trap_note: İstenen ile istenmeyeni değiştirir; kalıbın iki ucu takas edilince cümle karşıt bir eleştiri olur.

questions.stem: It is clear from the passage that Aristotle's objection to interest rested on ----.

options.o1: a claim about what money is by its nature able to do
options.o2: the religious traditions that later adopted the same prohibition
options.o3: the observation that borrowers were usually in distress
options.o4: the contracts that lawyers of his time were devising
options.o5: the rate at which lenders of the period were charging

questions.why: Parça gerekçeyi verir: para kısırdır ve üreyemez; itiraz paranın doğasına ilişkin bir savdır.
questions.trap_note: Sıralamayı tersine çevirir; dinî gelenekler yasağı paylaşır, ama Aristoteles'in gerekçesi onlardan gelmez.

questions.stem: According to the passage, the moral objection to interest lost its force because ----.

options.o1: the reason people borrowed money had changed
options.o2: theologians were persuaded by the lawyers' arguments
options.o3: the word usury came to mean something narrower
options.o4: lenders began to charge a lower rate of interest
options.o5: landlords stopped demanding debts from their tenants

questions.why: Parça bunu açıkça yazar: değişen ahlak değil, borçlanan kişidir; borç artık hayatta kalmak için değil, yatırım için alınmaktadır.
questions.trap_note: Parçanın sırasını tersine çevirir: hukukçular sonuca ilahiyatçılardan çok önce varmıştır.

questions.stem: It can be inferred from the passage that the contracts devised by lawyers ----.

options.o1: kept the prohibition in place while emptying it of effect
options.o2: were declared unlawful as soon as theologians examined them
options.o3: were used only in economies where borrowing was distress borrowing
options.o4: made borrowing considerably more expensive than it had been
options.o5: have disappeared entirely from the vocabulary of modern finance

questions.why: Sözleşmeler 'adı dışında her şeyiyle faiz'dir: yasak yerinde durur, işlevi kalmaz.
questions.trap_note: Parçanın tersini söyler; ilahiyatçılar bu sonucu çok sonra kabul etmiş, engellememiştir.

questions.stem: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.o1: A prohibition that fitted one kind of economy was narrowed rather than defeated as the economy changed.
options.o2: Religious law has had less influence on modern finance than is generally supposed.
options.o3: Aristotle's view of money was mistaken and was corrected by medieval lawyers.
options.o4: Lending at interest was universally condemned until the modern period began.
options.o5: The meaning of the word usury has been disputed for over two thousand years.

questions.why: Parça yasağın çöküşünü değil, daraltılışını anlatır ve son cümlede bunu açıkça söyler.
questions.trap_note: Parçanın ilgilenmediği bir karşılaştırmayı ana fikir yapar; metin etkinin büyüklüğünü değil, fikrin dönüşümünü izler.

questions.stem: According to the passage, burning the undergrowth had all of the following effects EXCEPT ----.

options.o1: removing the people who had lived in the forest
options.o2: keeping the forest open rather than crowded
options.o3: favouring the plants that game animals ate
options.o4: preventing the build-up that feeds a very large fire
options.o5: shaping the landscape over thousands of years

questions.why: Parçada yakmanın üç etkisi sayılır; insanların çıkarılması yakmanın sonucu değil, sonradan gelen ayrı bir olaydır.
questions.trap_note: Parçada açıkça sayılan bir etkidir; EXCEPT sorusunda doğru bilgiyi işaretlemek en sık yapılan hatadır.

questions.stem: It is clear from the passage that the parks began to burn as they had never burned before because ----.

options.o1: the policy of suppressing fire allowed the undergrowth to build up
options.o2: the climate of the region changed over the course of a century
options.o3: visitors to the parks were admitted in far greater numbers
options.o4: the original inhabitants set larger fires than the managers did
options.o5: controlled burning was reintroduced at considerable expense

questions.why: Parça zinciri kurar: yakma yasaklandı, çalılık geri geldi, yüzyıl içinde daha önce görülmemiş yangınlar çıktı.
questions.trap_note: Parçada hiç geçmeyen bir nedeni getirir; metin yangınları yönetim kararına bağlar.

questions.stem: It can be inferred from the passage that the writer objects to the word wilderness because ----.

options.o1: it promises that a place can be left alone when it cannot
options.o2: it is applied to land that has no ecological value
options.o3: it was invented by the people who removed the inhabitants
options.o4: it prevents controlled burning from being used at all
options.o5: it makes protected land seem less valuable than it is

questions.why: Son cümle itirazı verir: sözcük yerin kendi hâline bırakılabileceği vaadini taşır, oysa bu yerlerin çoğu bırakılamaz.
questions.trap_note: Parçanın açıkça reddettiği okumadır: metin korunan toprağın değerini savunur, tartıştığı şey adıdır.

questions.stem: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.o1: What is protected as untouched nature is mostly land that people made, and it needs managing rather than leaving alone.
options.o2: National parks should be returned to the people who were removed from them.
options.o3: Controlled burning is the only effective way of preventing large forest fires.
options.o4: Photographs taken in the early parks gave a false impression of their size.
options.o5: Protecting land does more harm than good wherever the policy is applied.

questions.why: Parça iki şeyi birlikte savunur: manzaranın insan eseri olduğu ve bunun korumayı bırakmayı değil, yönetmeyi gerektirdiği.
questions.trap_note: Parçanın vermediği siyasal sonuca atlar; metin bir mülkiyet önerisi değil, bir kavram eleştirisi yapar.

questions.stem: According to the passage, writing the rules down mattered because it made possible ----.

options.o1: a contest between people who had never met one another
options.o2: a version of the game that every village could agree was better
options.o3: the removal of the distinction between amateur and professional
options.o4: the fixing of the size of the pitch and the length of the match
options.o5: the employment of schoolmasters and clerks as officials

questions.why: Parça kodlamanın oyunu iyileştirmediğini, yabancılar arasında maçı olanaklı kıldığını açıkça söyler.
questions.trap_note: Kodlamayı bir iyileştirme sanır; parça bunu 'bir iyileştirme değil, bir koşul' diye ayırır.

questions.stem: It can be inferred from the passage that the length of a match and the number of players ----.

options.o1: could have been settled differently without harming the game
options.o2: were worked out from the requirements of the game itself
options.o3: have been revised more often than any other rule
options.o4: were the subject of disagreement for eighty years
options.o5: were fixed after the amateur rule had been abandoned

questions.why: Parça 'bunların hiçbiri oyundan çıkmaz' der: tek bir toplantının kararlarıdır, başka türlü de karara bağlanabilirlerdi.
questions.trap_note: Parçanın doğrudan reddettiği cümledir: 'None of these follows from the game.'

questions.stem: It is clear from the passage that the amateur rule was abandoned ----.

options.o1: once the money involved had become too large to ignore
options.o2: as soon as its origin in class was publicly admitted
options.o3: because schoolmasters and clerks no longer wrote the codes
options.o4: when the size of the pitch was revised for the last time
options.o5: after leagues and national teams had ceased to matter

questions.why: Parça vazgeçişin koşulunu verir: kalabalıklar önemsenecek kadar büyüyünce kural fazla tören yapılmadan bırakılmıştır.
questions.trap_note: Vazgeçişi bir itirafa bağlar; parçada kuralın sınıfsal kökeni yazarın saptamasıdır, dönemin kabulü değil.

questions.stem: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.o1: Modern sport rests on rules that were written for particular purposes and have since come to look like the nature of the game.
options.o2: Football would be a better game if its rules were revised by players rather than by committees.
options.o3: The amateur rule was the most damaging decision ever taken by a sporting body.
options.o4: Village football was more varied and more interesting than the codified game.
options.o5: Leagues and national teams could not have existed before the nineteenth century.

questions.why: Parça iki adımı izler: kuralların belirli amaçlarla yazılması ve zamanla oyunun kendisi sayılmaya başlanması.
questions.trap_note: Parçanın yapmadığı bir öneriyi ana fikir yapar; metin kuralların nasıl doğduğunu anlatır, nasıl değiştirileceğini değil.

questions.stem: It is clear from the passage that before the modern period prison was ----.

options.o1: a place of waiting rather than a punishment in itself
options.o2: the usual punishment for offences too small for a fine
options.o3: reserved for those who could not pay what they owed
options.o4: administered by the same officials who carried out whippings
options.o5: avoided because the state could not afford to guard it

questions.why: Parçanın ilk iki cümlesi bunu söyler: hapis, yargılanmayı ya da cezanın kendisini bekleme yeridir.
questions.trap_note: Hapsi bir ceza türü sayar; parça tam da bunun modern bir fikir olduğunu anlatmaktadır.

questions.stem: According to the passage, a sentence measured in years would have meant little in an earlier society because ----.

options.o1: time was not yet counted in the units such a sentence assumes
options.o2: courts of the period did not keep written records of their decisions
options.o3: prisoners were released whenever the prison became too full
options.o4: the state preferred punishments that could be carried out at once
options.o5: nobody could be certain how long an accused person would live

questions.why: Parça ikinci koşulu ayrıca vurgular: saat, takvim ve haftalık ücret olmadan dört yıl neredeyse hiçbir şey ifade etmez.
questions.trap_note: Kayıt tutmayı gerekçe yapar; parçada kayıt hapsin bir üstünlüğü olarak anılır, önkoşulu olarak değil.

questions.stem: It can be inferred from the passage that the two objections to imprisonment ----.

options.o1: have not been answered by anything that has happened since
options.o2: were met by allowing sentences to be appealed and reduced
options.o3: are raised chiefly by those who prefer corporal punishment
options.o4: apply equally to the fine and to transportation
options.o5: were first made after the system had been in place for a century

questions.why: Parça iki itirazın da ayakta kaldığını söyler ve son cümlede iki yüzyılın sessizliği dolduramadığını ekler.
questions.trap_note: İtiraz ile idari kolaylığı karıştırır; itiraz edilebilmesi, birimin eşitsizliğine ya da amaçsızlığına yanıt değildir.

questions.stem: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.o1: Punishment by time is a recent invention that is exact about how much and silent about what for.
options.o2: Imprisonment is more humane than the punishments that preceded it and should be retained.
options.o3: The length of a sentence should be adjusted according to the age of the offender.
options.o4: Prisons became possible only when states grew rich enough to build them.
options.o5: Corporal punishment was abandoned because it could not be recorded.

questions.why: Parça hem fikrin yeniliğini hem de niceliğe kesin, amaca sessiz oluşunu birlikte kurar.
questions.trap_note: Parçadaki bir gözlemi savunmaya çevirir; metin insanilik iddiasını yayılma nedeni olarak anar, kendi savı olarak değil.

questions.stem: According to the passage, limited liability had two consequences, the second of which was that ----.

options.o1: money could be raised for an enterprise that did not exist
options.o2: investors were able to supervise the firms they had financed
options.o3: auditors were required to certify every set of accounts
options.o4: companies were forbidden to collapse without an inquiry
options.o5: promoters had to put in as much money as they raised

questions.why: Parça aynı özelliğin iki yüzünü verir: yabancılar denetleyemedikleri bir işi finanse edebilir, aynı nedenle var olmayan bir iş için para toplanabilir.
questions.trap_note: Parçanın tersini söyler: yatırımcıların denetleyememesi, sorunun kaynağı olarak anılır.

questions.stem: It is clear from the passage that published accounts answer well ----.

options.o1: the question that the nineteenth-century collapses had raised
options.o2: the question of whether a business is being well run
options.o3: the questions that auditors are most often asked by readers
options.o4: every question that a demand for disclosure has produced
options.o5: the question of why a firm's records were kept as they were

questions.why: Parça ayrımı açıkça kurar: hesaplar 'para yerinde mi' sorusuna iyi yanıt verir, iyi yönetilip yönetilmediğine neredeyse hiç.
questions.trap_note: Parçanın yanıtlanmadığını söylediği soruyu yanıtlanan soru sanır.

questions.stem: It can be inferred from the passage that the writer regards the usual response to a scandal as ----.

options.o1: an increase in quantity where a change of question was needed
options.o2: the only remedy available to a regulator after a collapse
options.o3: an attack on auditors who had done nothing wrong
options.o4: a sign that limited liability should be abolished
options.o5: evidence that readers understand the reports very well

questions.why: Son cümle iki seçeneği karşı karşıya koyar: daha fazla açıklama istendi, farklı türden bir soru değil.
questions.trap_note: Yazarın eleştirdiği tepkiyi tek olanak sayar; oysa cümlede açıkça bir alternatif adlandırılmaktadır.

questions.stem: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.o1: Company accounts answer the question that produced them, and are persistently read as answering a larger one.
options.o2: Auditors have been responsible for most of the financial scandals of the last century.
options.o3: Limited liability should never have been extended to companies financed by strangers.
options.o4: Disclosure requirements have grown steadily more detailed since the nineteenth century.
options.o5: A firm that satisfies every legal requirement can nevertheless be a sound investment.

questions.why: Parça hesapların kökenini, ne yanıtladığını ve ne yanıtlamadığını izler; ana fikir bu boşluktur.
questions.trap_note: Boşluğun sorumluluğunu denetçilere yükler; parça ise belgenin kapsamı ile beklenti arasındaki farkı anlatır.

dialogue: You say the old ban on lending at interest was never really defeated.
That sounds like a distinction without a difference.

It is not, because the shape of the detour is still there. Half the instruments a bank will sell you were designed to be something other than a loan, and they were designed that way by people answering to a rule nobody now remembers.

options.o1: It was got around. That is a different thing from being repealed.
options.o2: It was repealed, and a good deal earlier than most people suppose.
options.o3: It was never actually in force outside a handful of European cities.
options.o4: It was defeated by the followers of Aristotle in the sixteenth century.
options.o5: It survives today in the meaning we give to the word usury.

questions.why: Sunucu 'farksız bir ayrım' der; bu itiraz ancak iki şeyin ayrıldığı bir cümleden sonra gelebilir.
questions.trap_note: Tarihçinin savını ortadan kaldırır: yasak kaldırıldıysa ortada tartışılacak bir ayrım kalmaz.

dialogue: You spend a considerable budget setting fire to a forest that you are paid to protect.
We spend it putting back something that was taken out. This forest was burned every few years for thousands of years, and then it was not, for about a hundred.
And that hundred years of protection is what caused the problem?

options.o1: It produced a forest that had never existed before, and then that forest caught fire.
options.o2: No, the problem is the climate, and there is very little we can do about that.
options.o3: Protection has in fact worked exactly as it was intended to work.
options.o4: The people who used to burn it left the area of their own accord.
options.o5: We shall know in another hundred years, and not before then.

questions.why: Soru doğrudan sorulmuştur ve yanıt ilk repliğin savını tamamlamalıdır: koruma yeni bir orman üretmiş, yangın da onu bulmuştur.
questions.trap_note: Yöneticinin bir önceki replikte kurduğu açıklamayı reddeder; kendi bütçesini savunan biri bunu söylemez.

dialogue: Because a committee decided it in an afternoon, and then a hundred years went by. There is nothing in the game itself that requires eleven rather than ten or twelve.
Somebody must have had a reason at the time.

Probably the number of boys in a boarding house. That is the level at which most of these things were settled, and it is why they are so hard to change now: an arbitrary rule kept for a century stops looking arbitrary.

options.o1: Why are there eleven players in a football team rather than some other number?
options.o2: Why has the number of players in a football team been changed so often?
options.o3: Who were the men who first wrote the rules of the game down?
options.o4: When did football first come to be played between different villages?
options.o5: How long did it take for the written rules to be accepted everywhere?

questions.why: Yanıt 'on bir yerine on ya da on iki' der ve bir sayının neden öyle olduğunu açıklar; boşluk bu sayıyı soran cümledir.
questions.trap_note: Sayının sık değiştiğini varsayar; oysa yanıt bir yüzyıldır hiç değişmediğini anlatmaktadır.

dialogue: If you could change one thing about sentencing, what would it be?
I would make the court say what the sentence is for. Not the offence, the purpose. Four years for what?
Then we should have to admit that we do not know, which would be a considerable advance on saying a number and looking satisfied.

options.o1: And what if the court turned out to be unable to answer that?
options.o2: And would the sentences then be shorter than they are at present?
options.o3: Do the prisoners themselves ever ask you what it is for?
options.o4: Has any country tried writing the purpose into the sentence?
options.o5: How long have you been arguing for this particular change?

questions.why: Yanıt 'o zaman bilmediğimizi kabul etmek zorunda kalırdık' der; boşluk mahkemenin yanıtsız kalması ihtimalini sormalıdır.
questions.trap_note: Süreyi sorar; yanıtın tamamı ise sürenin uzunluğuyla değil, amacın bilinmemesiyle ilgilidir.

dialogue: Your signature is on the accounts of a company that failed four months later. How does that happen?
Readers do not make that distinction.

No, and we have not worked very hard to teach them. A report saying that the figures match the books is read as a report saying that the company is sound, and the two have almost nothing to do with each other.

options.o1: Because what I signed was not a statement that the company would survive.
options.o2: Because the figures in those accounts turned out later to have been falsified.
options.o3: Because the collapse came from a part of the business we never examine.
options.o4: Because four months is quite long enough for almost anything to go wrong.
options.o5: Because the inquiry has not yet reported and I am unable to comment.

questions.why: Sunucunun 'okurlar bu ayrımı yapmaz' demesi, bir önceki repliğin iki şeyi ayırmış olmasını gerektirir.
questions.trap_note: Ortada bir ayrım bırakmaz: rakamlar sahteyse sorun okurun yorumu değil, denetimin kendisidir.

questions.stem: Only when the borrower ceased to be somebody staving off ruin did the objection to interest begin to lose its force.

options.o1: The objection to interest began to weaken only once borrowers were no longer people trying to stave off ruin.
options.o2: The objection to interest began to weaken well before borrowers stopped being people trying to stave off ruin.
options.o3: Borrowers stopped trying to stave off ruin because the objection to interest had weakened.
options.o4: The objection to interest was strongest among those borrowers who were closest to ruin.
options.o5: Only borrowers who were facing ruin went on objecting to being charged interest.

questions.why: Only when + devrik yapı bir koşul sırası kurar: itiraz ancak borçlunun değişmesinden sonra zayıflamıştır.
questions.trap_note: Sırayı bozar; 'ancak o zaman' ifadesini 'çok önce' diye okuyunca iki olayın ilişkisi kalmaz.

questions.stem: Far from being untouched, the land now protected as wilderness was shaped by people for thousands of years.

options.o1: The land now protected as wilderness, so far from being untouched, was shaped by people over thousands of years.
options.o2: The land now protected as wilderness was untouched until people began to shape it thousands of years ago.
options.o3: Land that people have shaped for thousands of years cannot properly be protected as wilderness.
options.o4: Only land that has never been touched by people ought to be called wilderness at all.
options.o5: The protection of wilderness began thousands of years after the land had been shaped.

questions.why: Far from + ulaç, beklenenin tam tersini bildirir: dokunulmamış olmak şöyle dursun, toprak binlerce yıl biçimlendirilmiştir.
questions.trap_note: Kalıbı bir zaman sırasına çevirir ve toprağa önce dokunulmamış bir dönem uydurur.

questions.stem: Not until a society counted time in weeks and wages could a sentence of four years mean anything to the person receiving it.

options.o1: A sentence of four years could mean something to the person receiving it only once a society counted time in weeks and wages.
options.o2: A society began counting time in weeks and wages only after sentences of four years had come to mean something.
options.o3: Sentences of four years were introduced in societies that did not yet count time in weeks and wages.
options.o4: Nobody who received a sentence of four years has ever properly understood what it meant.
options.o5: Counting time in weeks and wages made sentences of four years unnecessary.

questions.why: Not until + devrik yapı önkoşul bildirir: haftayla ve ücretle ölçülen bir zaman olmadan dört yıl bir şey ifade etmez.
questions.trap_note: Koşul ile sonucu değiştirir; hangisinin önce geldiği tersine dönünce cümlenin savı yok olur.

questions.stem: It is not that the auditor's report says too little; it is that it is read as saying a great deal more.

options.o1: The trouble lies not in how little the auditor's report says but in how much more it is taken to say.
options.o2: The trouble lies not in how much the auditor's report is taken to say but in how little it actually says.
options.o3: The auditor's report says too little and is read as saying too little as well.
options.o4: Readers of the auditor's report understand quite precisely how narrow its claim is.
options.o5: The auditor's report would be a good deal more useful if it said rather less.

questions.why: It is not that A; it is that B kalıbı sorunu B'ye yerleştirir: kusur raporun darlığında değil, okunuşundadır.
questions.trap_note: Kalıbın iki ucunu değiştirir ve sorunu tam da yazarın dışladığı yere koyar.

questions.stem: Libraries that abolished their fines expected to lose books and found that they did not. ---- Almost everybody who keeps a book late brings it back in the end; the people the fine removed were the ones who stopped coming at all, because a debt of four pounds is a reason to avoid a building. What the fine collected was a small sum from the borrowers who could pay it and the permanent absence of those who could not.

options.o1: The fine had never been doing the work it was thought to do.
options.o2: Most of the missing books came back within a month of the change.
options.o3: Fines were introduced in the nineteenth century to pay for replacements.
options.o4: Librarians had been arguing about the question for a generation.
options.o5: Some libraries kept the charge for films and recorded music.

questions.why: Boşluktan sonrası cezanın neyi topladığını ve kimi uzaklaştırdığını anlatır; boşluk, cezanın sanılan işlevi görmediğini söylemelidir.
questions.trap_note: Beklenmeyen sonucu bir ayrıntıyla açıklar; paragraf ise cezanın işlevine ilişkin genel bir yargıya gider.

questions.stem: A district that has kept its nineteenth-century buildings is usually a district that could not afford to knock them down. ---- Prosperity destroys old streets a great deal more efficiently than neglect does, and the places praised today for their character are often places that were passed over when there was money to spend. This is awkward for conservation, because the thing now being preserved was produced by exactly the condition everybody is trying to bring to an end.

options.o1: Preservation, in other words, is frequently an accident of poverty.
options.o2: Conservation law has protected these streets since the 1960s.
options.o3: Victorian building methods were sounder than those that followed.
options.o4: Most such districts are now expensive places in which to live.
options.o5: Architects have long admired the proportions of these terraces.

questions.why: Boşluk, ilk cümledeki gözlemi bir kurala çevirmelidir: korunmuşluk çoğu kez yoksulluğun yan ürünüdür.
questions.trap_note: Korunmayı hukuka bağlar; paragraf ise binaların yasadan önce, para olmadığı için ayakta kaldığını söyler.

questions.stem: A restaurant that prints the bare number 24 on its menu where it might have printed twenty-four pounds is not saving ink. ---- The research on this is unusually consistent: diners spend more when the symbol is absent, and more again when the prices are not lined up in a column, because a column invites comparison and comparison invites the cheapest dish. None of it is hidden; it is printed on every menu in the country and almost nobody sees it.

options.o1: It is removing a reminder that money is being spent.
options.o2: It is following a design fashion that began in the 1990s.
options.o3: Most menus are redesigned once or twice in a year.
options.o4: Diners rarely remember the following day what they paid.
options.o5: The cheapest dish is usually the second cheapest on the list.

questions.why: Boşluktan sonraki araştırma, işaretin yokluğunun harcamayı artırdığını söyler; boşluk bunun nedenini adlandırmalıdır.
questions.trap_note: Bir tasarım açıklaması verir; paragraf ise etkinin ölçülmüş olduğunu ve amacın harcama olduğunu anlatır.

questions.stem: An obituary is the only kind of journalism written about somebody who cannot object to it, and the profession treats this as a licence rather than a difficulty. ---- Most are drafted years in advance, filed, and brought up to date at intervals by people who will never meet the subject, which is why the good ones read as though the writer had been waiting patiently and the bad ones as though a cupboard had been opened. What the form is really for is not the dead, who are beyond flattery, but the living, who are being told what a life of that kind amounts to.

options.o1: The work, in any case, is done long before it is needed.
options.o2: Relatives are consulted before publication in almost every case.
options.o3: Newspapers devote rather less space to them than they once did.
options.o4: The form has changed very little in a hundred and fifty years.
options.o5: Some subjects have been known to read their own by mistake.

questions.why: Boşluktan sonra yıllar önce yazılıp dosyalanan metinler anlatılır; boşluk bu üretim biçimini haber vermelidir.
questions.trap_note: Paragrafın hemen ardından gelen 'kimseyle tanışmayan yazarlar' ifadesiyle çelişir.

sentences: The shopping trolley was rejected by customers for several years after it was introduced in the 1930s.
Men thought it looked like a pram, and women said they had pushed quite enough prams already.
The inventor hired actors to walk round his shops pushing loaded trolleys until the objection wore off.
Supermarkets in Europe adopted self-service checkouts a good deal later than American ones did.
The trolley then did what it had been designed to do, which was to make the limit on a purchase the customer's money rather than the customer's arms.
questions.why: IV. cümle kasa teknolojisine geçer; paragraf ise alışveriş arabasının nasıl reddedilip nasıl kabul ettirildiğini anlatır.
questions.trap_note: I. cümle yalnızca bir tarih veriyor gibi görünür ama paragrafın anlattığı direnişi kuran cümledir.

sentences: Britain introduced a driving test in 1935, some forty years after the first cars had appeared on its roads.
The internal combustion engine had been patented in the 1880s.
For those four decades anybody who could buy a car was free to drive one, and the casualty figures of the period are higher than today's with a fraction of the traffic.
The test was opposed on the ground that driving was a matter of common sense and could not be examined.
It was introduced in spite of that, and the figures fell within three years.
questions.why: II. cümle motorun patentine geçer; paragrafın konusu sürücü sınavının gecikmesi ve etkisidir.
questions.trap_note: IV. cümle karşı görüşü aktardığı için konu dışı sanılır; oysa sınavın 'buna rağmen' getirildiğini anlatan halkadır.

sentences: Houses in European cities were not numbered until governments needed to find the people inside them.
The first systematic numbering was carried out for conscription and for taxation, not for the convenience of visitors.
Residents understood this perfectly well, and in several cities they tore the numbers down as fast as they were painted on.
Most of these cities had walls that were pulled down during the same period.
What is now a neutral piece of information began as an instrument of the state and was resisted as one.
questions.why: IV. cümle surların yıkılmasına geçer; paragrafın izlediği şey numaraların neden konduğu ve neden söküldüğüdür.
questions.trap_note: I. cümle genel bir giriş gibi durur ama paragrafın bütün savı orada kurulan 'devlet aradığı için' fikrine dayanır.

sentences: Until the end of the eighteenth century a woman's pocket was a separate bag tied round the waist under the skirt.
When fashion narrowed the skirt the pocket had nowhere left to go, so it left the clothing altogether and became the handbag.
Silk was replaced by cotton in much of European dressmaking during the same decades.
What had been a private space inside the clothes became an object that could be taken, forgotten or searched.
Campaigns for pockets in women's clothing have been running, on and off, ever since.
questions.why: III. cümle kumaş değişimine geçer; paragraf ise cebin giysiden çıkıp çantaya dönüşmesini ve bunun sonucunu anlatır.
questions.trap_note: II. cümle moda ayrıntısı gibi görünür ama cebin giysiden ayrılışını anlatan halkadır.

sentences: Hospitals restricted visiting to an hour a week for most of the twentieth century and defended the rule as a matter of infection control.
Antibiotics became widely available in the years immediately after the Second World War.
The evidence for the rule was thin, and the evidence against it, once anybody troubled to look, was not: patients who were visited recovered faster and went home sooner.
The rule survived because it was convenient for the ward rather than because it was good for the patient.
Where it has been abandoned, nothing that was predicted has actually happened.
questions.why: II. cümle antibiyotiklerin yayılmasına geçer; paragrafın konusu ziyaret kuralının dayanağı ve kaderidir.
questions.trap_note: IV. cümle kuralı açıkladığı için sapma sanılır; oysa paragrafın vardığı yargının kendisidir.

vocabulary: raise (the question the collapses had raised)
saving (the savings a factory would find)
